# Pending changes (since patch 0022, 2026-11-24)

## 2026-11-24 - The browser game in seconds, smooth from the first frame
Asked: "45 seconds is too much, reduce it down to a few seconds, load the game while the game plays ... use much lower resolution objects as placeholders until the higher resolution ones are loaded. Use threading properly so nothing stutters and freezes ... test this thoroughly on the web browser". Measured in Chromium throughout (the web export served locally; frames per second and the longest frame each second from the page; the load's steps timed in the console).
- Start game -> in the game: was 15-140 s (45 s on itch); now ~6-7 s, every time.
- Your ship's hull and rooms were waited for before the scene went on - in a new game you have no ship, and in a browser those jobs took 40 s+ behind others. Now the ship comes in at once with a plain stand-in for its hull (its size, the hull's material) and no rooms; the real hull and rooms go in when their workers finish (CosmosShip.parts_in, polled by Cosmos); boarding finishes them on the spot (CosmosWalker.set_deck). In a browser they're only built once you have a ship; the desktop still waits for them (a moment there, no mesh swapped in during play).
- The title's background loads (the scene, you, the start city's people) are waited for a frame at a time before the build (CosmosWarm.loads_done) - a load() of one still loading had stopped a frame for a second; the rest (other people, menus) asked for only once those are in. In a browser, scripts and the scenes made of them (player data, missions, the HUD, the menus) are loaded on the main thread a thing a frame under the loading screen (CosmosWarm.load_direct): loaded on a thread there, each script waits on the main thread step by step - the HUD with all it uses took ~30 s. UI.switch_scene waits for a scene still loading in the background.
- In a browser, what's seen first is drawn once under the loading screen (you, the townspeople, the town's buildings, plants, creatures, deposits: CosmosWarm.draw_in) - else each first draw stopped play a fifth of a second as it came into view.
- Heavy background jobs (towns, ship designs, hulls, rooms, stations' bakes, dungeons, monsters, traders' rooms) go through Jobs (scripts/core/jobs.gd): on the desktop the pool's own tasks; in a browser the low-priority ones one at a time. The ships' designs in a browser start one at a time once the game's in (EmpireHulls.pump).
- The real cause of ~40 FPS for 10-20 s after arriving in a browser: the 2D art loader (ProcArt) still had ~740 pictures queued, decoding 8 ms of them on the main thread each frame. In the 3D game in a browser it now loads only pictures asked for (their placeholders shown a frame or two); the rest load at the title. After arriving: 60 FPS, worst frame ~40 ms (was ~200 ms hitches).
- A town's meshes are put in one block a frame (each a GPU upload - all at once a long frame in a browser).
- The web build's threads: the low-priority share 0.6 (project setting; was 0.3).
- The builds: the old 2D game's clip sheets (art/player_clips, art/pirate_clips - nothing uses them) left out of every export: the web download 188 -> ~154 MB.
Desktop: the FPS tour unchanged (the hangar below its baseline as before); the Hyperion drive's long frame gone (11 ms, was ~85 ms).
Files: scripts/core/jobs.gd (new), scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_ship.gd, cosmos_ship_interior.gd, cosmos_walker.gd, scripts/world/models/cosmos_warm.gd, empire_hulls.gd, scripts/world/life/cosmos_town.gd, cosmos_dungeon.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos_monster.gd, cosmos_npc_interior.gd, cosmos_station.gd, scripts/world/build/cosmos_structure.gd, scripts/core/proc_art.gd, scripts/ui/ui.gd, project.godot, export_presets.cfg; guide shots retaken.
- Menus' first opening in a browser: the Automaton's screen made under the loading screen and its inventory page shown once there (Cosmos._make_computer) - its first opening in play was a 0.42 s frame, now ~0.07 s; the planet map's first opening 0.21 -> ~0.12 s.
Tested in Chromium (served locally): Start game -> playing in 6-7 s (three runs); after that ~60 FPS average, walking 12 s with the terrain streaming in at ~60 FPS, opening the inventory and the planet map; no script errors.

## 2026-11-24 - Smooth turning and animation: no snaps, no jumps
Asked: "blender animations better, for example the automaton turning back to front is too sudden, left and right the same. Make sure all animations are smooth with no sudden jumps to new animations".
- Turning: the automaton turned with an exponential blend (90% of a turn in ~0.2 s) and SNAPPED round when reversing (a new way more than ~179 degrees off). New SmoothTurn (scripts/world/life/smooth_turn.gd): a turn speed that builds up, is held at a top rate and eases off as it comes round; a reversal goes round one side (the side it's turning, else the right) - in the game a reversal is now a 180-degree turn over ~0.55 s, at most 7 degrees a frame (measured live). Used by the walker (aiming a quicker one), the townspeople and the creatures (each with its own rates). Seated station crew eased onto their seats and round (were set in one frame).
- Clips cross-faded longer: the walker 0.3 s (a jump's spring 0.12 s; BLENDS), the townspeople 0.3 s (were 0.18 / 0.15). A reversal passing through still keeps its stride (standing only after 0.15 s still) - no flick to standing and back.
- Loop seams: the imported clips end ON their last frame (length (n-1)/fps), so each loop jumped from the last frame straight to the first - up to 20 degrees a step in the run, 17 in the swim. Stage3D.loop_clips sets every looping clip (model.json "loop") to loop and n/fps long (its last frame blending into its first): the walker, the townspeople, the hangar crew, the menus' model view.
- Clip glitches mended as they load (Stage3D.smooth_clips, once a model, its clips shared): a bone flipping away for 1-4 frames and straight back (the pose solver's other solution: up to 180 degrees a frame - the dive's shoulder pieces, the leap, the knockout, the swim's 75-degree spike) has those frames blended across; a pose jumping in one frame (over 60 degrees in a looping clip, 100 in another, and 2.5x the motion round it) is spread over the frames either side. Player: 94 frames mended, flips over 120 degrees 19 -> 0; every other character 24-51 mended, all to 0. Done in the warm-ups (the title on the desktop, under the loading screen in a browser), ~4-8 ms a model.
- Tests: tests/test_animation.gd (a reversal smooth, one way round, never over the top speed a frame; looping clips a whole cycle; no flips over 120 degrees in any model; the cross-fades).
Files: scripts/world/life/smooth_turn.gd (new), scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, scripts/world/life/cosmos_npc.gd, cosmos_creature.gd, scripts/world/station/cosmos_hangar.gd, scripts/world/models/stage3d.gd, cosmos_warm.gd, scripts/ui/model_view.gd, tests/test_animation.gd; guide shots retaken.

## 2026-11-24 - The rifle: slung on the back, drawn, aimed where the shots go, slung back
Asked: "the animation of take out the gun and the putting it back in is bad, improve it and make more realistic, also it does not correctly point the gun towards the direction the bullet is fired".
- Why it looked bad: in every clip without the rifle it was parked 5 m under the floor, out of sight - so the cross-fade into the rifle clips drew it up out of the ground into the hands (and sank it back). And shooting played the CARRY pose (gun_idle: the barrel ~45 degrees left and down) while the bolts flew from a fixed point to the sights.
- Blender (external/blender/automaton): the automaton's rifle slung across its back in every clip without it (moves.STOW: the grip low on the left of the back, the barrel up past the right shoulder, outside the jet pack; kit.py: a rifle with no hand on it, hands "none"); two new clips - draw (0.53 s: the right hand up behind the shoulder, the rifle slid up along its slant into it, swung over the shoulder to the front, the left hand meeting it) and holster (0.6 s, the other way). The player re-exported (46 clips; the user's overrides merged as before - Head, Torso, Arm.L/R, Leg.L/R; no problems).
- In the game: ArmsLayer (scripts/world/player/arms_layer.gd, a SkeletonModifier3D) plays the upper body - spine, chest, head, arms, rifle - over whatever the legs do (walking, running, standing), the spine set so the chest lands where the clip has it whatever the legs' pelvis does, the rifle carried with the pelvis's bob; it cross-fades between its clips. The walker's rifle: slung -> drawing (when you shoot or mine; the shots wait for it) -> aiming (the "fire" clip's aim pose, its recoil each shot; the chest - and the rifle round it - pitched up or down to the aim point; the body turned to where the shots go) -> carry (0.8 s after the last shot) -> holstering (when it's no longer wanted, 3 s) -> slung; each eased in and out. Bolts leave from the rifle's own muzzle (as posed, with the layer). Measured live: the barrel along the shot within 2-6 degrees standing or walking (was 52).
- Test: test_cosmos.test_rifle_drawn_aimed_slung (slung behind the back, drawn then aimed, no shot while drawing, the barrel along the shot, the shot from the muzzle, slung back).
Files: external/blender/automaton/kit.py, moves.py (backups in external/blender/automaton/backup/), art/player_3d/player.glb + model.json, scripts/world/player/arms_layer.gd (new), scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd; guide shots retaken.

## 2026-11-24 - Patch Notes on the title screen, no SVG editor, mods and the Mod Editor

Asked: move the Patcher out of Talos into its own entry on the main menu ("Patch Notes"); remove the SVG
editor completely; add a mesh editor (with proportional editing, a mirror modifier and symmetry tools) and an
animation editor; support mods that can change anything in the game, with a standalone mod editor.

- **Patch Notes**: the Patcher is no longer a Talos tool (off the rail, F7 freed). The title screen and the
  Esc menu have **Patch Notes**: it opens over the menu on a layer of its own (Patcher.open_over), running
  while a game is paused under it; Back / Esc closes it. Header "PATCH NOTES", a Back button.
- **The SVG editor removed**: scripts/editor/svg_editor.gd (1,889 lines), svg_doc.gd (691), its scene, its
  icon, its F6 key, its chapter of the Talos manual, its drawings (art/svg: 3 files, only it used them).
- **Talos's rail**: the data editor's pages, then **Meshes** (F6) and **Animation** (F7) - the two new tools.
- **Mods** (scripts/core/mods.gd, the first autoload - before Settings): a mod is user://mods/<id>/ -
  mod.json (name, version, author, description, main) + files/ laid out like res://. A file the game has is
  replaced, a new one added; `<file>.json.merge` deep-merges into the game's JSON (key by key, two mods can
  patch one file); "main" - the mod's own script, a Node added to the root once the game's up.
  How: every turned-on mod's files (and the merged JSON) packed into one zip (rebuilt only when a mod's files
  change) and mounted over res:// (load_resource_pack: what's read as files and listed), plus a
  ResourceFormatLoader in front of Godot's own loading what's load()ed from the mod's raw files - scripts
  from source, scenes/resources/shaders, pictures, glTF models, ogg/wav/mp3, fonts (an exported game knows
  only its imported copies). Load order: later wins. Safe start: a start that never reaches the title screen
  leaves a mark - the next runs without mods and says so; `--no-mods` too.
- **Mods screen** (title screen > Mods; scripts/ui/mods_screen.gd): every mod, on/off, load order (Earlier /
  Later), files changed by two mods flagged, Install (zip), Export (zip), Folder, Delete, Edit, Restart to apply.
- **The Mod Editor** (scenes/editor/mod_editor.tscn, scripts/editor/mod_editor.gd; Mods > Mod Editor, or
  standalone: `-- --mod-editor`): the game's files (searchable) - Override (copy into the mod: raw file, or
  in an export rebuilt from what loads - a picture as PNG, a model as GLB), Merge patch; the mod's files
  (replacing / new / merged in colour); text, data, scripts, scenes, shaders in a code editor with
  highlighting, checked on save (JSON parses, scripts compile); pictures previewed, sounds played, models to
  the mesh editor, Replace from a file; New file, Main script (from a template), Remove; Check (the whole
  mod), Test in game (F5: on + restart), Export; tabs MESHES / ANIMATION embed Talos's editors saving into
  the mod (EditTarget, scripts/editor/edit_target.gd - where the tools save: the game or the mod).
- Docs: Talos manual - the overview, rail, keys; the SVG chapter removed; "Patch Notes"; a new "Mods"
  chapter (mods, what a mod is, the Mod Editor). Archive blurbs. CLAUDE.md.
- Tests: tests/test_mods.gd (5): deep merge; list/order/zip round trip; **a real start of the game with a mod**
  (a child Godot: merge patch applied, a new script loads, a replaced picture 7x5, its main script ran);
  the Mod Editor (override, merge patch, new file, main script, checks); the Mods screen and Patch Notes,
  Talos without SVG/Versions.
- Note: exported builds compile scripts (script_export_mode=2), so the Mod Editor can't copy a script's source
  in an export - a mod writes its own version (or the game could ship text scripts).

Files: project.godot (Mods autoload), scripts/core/mods.gd (new), scripts/editor/edit_target.gd (new),
scripts/editor/mod_editor.gd (new), scenes/editor/mod_editor.tscn (new), scripts/ui/mods_screen.gd (new),

## 2026-11-24 - The mesh editor and the animation editor (Talos)

- **Meshes** (Talos, F6; scenes/editor/mesh_editor.tscn, scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd 2,097 lines + mesh/edit_mesh.gd
  1,069, mesh/mesh_view.gd 387, mesh/mesh_io.gd 274): the game's models and your own - glb/gltf, OBJ, .tres/.res
  meshes, new from primitives; its own lit 3D view (orbit, pan, zoom, numpad views, ortho, frame). Object mode: parts
  tree, click select, G/R/S with axis locks, fields, six primitives, duplicate/delete/rename. Edit mode (Tab): vertex /
  edge / face (1/2/3), click / shift / box select, G/R/S, extrude, delete, merge, subdivide (no cracks), flip and
  recalc normals; coincident points welded for editing; bone weights kept (new points mix theirs). **Proportional
  editing** (O; radius by wheel / Page Up/Down / field; smooth, sphere, root, linear, sharp, constant; connected only -
  along edges; its circle drawn). **Mirror modifier** (X/Y/Z, clip at the seam, merge distance; live as mirrored copies;
  applied on save or Apply). **Symmetry** (X/Y/Z twin editing; Symmetrize +X->-X or back). Materials per surface (the
  model's own, 11 game looks, colour/metal/roughness/glow). Undo/redo. Saves GLB through EditTarget (game or mod);
  saving over a Blender-made character in the game asks first.
  Numbers (the Minoan body: 11,865 points, 42,024 faces): edit mode ready in 60-70 ms (a worker); a drag ~6 ms a frame
  with ~9,900 points under proportional editing; mirror applied on save ~320 ms. Tests: tests/test_mesh_editor.gd (7).
- **Animation** (Talos, F7; scenes/editor/anim_editor.tscn, scripts/editor/anim_editor.gd ~1,760 lines): a character
  (every model Stage3D has) as in game, its skeleton drawn over it; clips list; timeline (play, speed, loop, frame
  and key stepping, scrub) and a dope sheet (bones x frames: select, drag, copy/paste keys and poses, delete);
  posing (click a bone; R turn with X/Y/Z axis, G move; fields; key bone K / all Shift+K; auto-key); easing per bone
  track (linear / smooth / step); clips new / copy / rename (your own) / delete / length / loop; onion skin; undo.
  Saves each clip as art/<id>_3d/clips/<clip>.tres (game or mod); Stage3D puts clip files in place of / beside a
  model's clips wherever characters get their clips (shared libraries: every instance, the arms layer too) - one
  folder check per model, nothing per frame. Tests: tests/test_anim_editor.gd (4).
- The Mod Editor's MESHES / ANIMATION tabs embed them (saving into the mod).

## 2026-11-24 - The Live Editor: edit anything while the game runs

Asked: "I want to be able to edit everything while the game is running: models, textures, animations, particle
effects, collisions etc."

- **The Live Editor** (F10 in a game - Keybinds "live_edit"; scripts/world/live/live_editor.gd): a panel down the
  right of the running game (Pause, speed 0.1-2x). Click anything in the world: picked by its triangles (each mesh's
  TriangleMesh, cached), a scatter as a whole; its box drawn; Up / its parts. Tabs are plug-ins
  (scripts/world/live/tabs/<id>_tab.gd: handles / bind / unbind / live_process / static apply_edit):
  - **Object**: place, turn, size, shown, shadow, see-through, and its script's own values - live, refreshed.
  - **Model**: its meshes - a copy opened in the mesh editor in a window over the game, "Put in the world"; Replace
    with a model file; As made.
  - **Materials**: every shader parameter (ranges as sliders, colours, vectors, textures) or a standard material's;
    per-instance values; Its own copy; textures replaced from pictures.
  - **Animation**: its clips - play any now, its speed; the animation editor in a window on its character and clip.
  - **Collision** (scripts/world/live/tabs/collision_tab.gd + solids_edit.gd): every box-based solid system - towns
    and your structures (CosmosSolids: AABBs, turned boxes as prisms), stations (oriented boxes, cylinders),
    dungeons, hangars (camera boxes and footprints), NPC ship interiors: drawn as lines (60 m round; through walls
    optional), picked by a click, moved / sized / turned / switched off, added, copied, deleted, reverted - live:
    the walker and camera meet the new boxes at once. Kept as the changes from the place as built (so it applies
    once, however often). Each builder calls SolidsEdit.installed() as it installs its solids (one lookup a build).
  - **Particles**: see the effects entry.
- **Kept edits** (scripts/world/live/live_edits.gd): most of the world is made in code, so an edit is kept against
  the kind of thing it was made on (its key: a builder's meta "edit_key" - town/<empire>/<kind>/<seed>,
  station/<empire>/<id>, dungeon/<style>/<seed>, hangar/..., interior/... - or its script's file: "every Cosmos
  Ship") and its part's path, in data/live_edits.json, and put back as each such thing is made (and again at 0.6 /
  2.5 / 8 s for parts built later). An edit spreads to the others of its kind in the world at once. Save: into the
  game or a mod (EditTarget); new meshes as art/live/<kind>/<part>.res, pictures as art/live/tex/*.png. A mod can
  carry data/live_edits.json(.merge) like any data file.
- Characters carry meta "model_id" (CosmosModels.apply) - which model a body is.
- Docs: a "Live Editor" chapter (live, live-object, live-model, live-materials, live-anim, live-collision); keys.
- Tests: tests/test_live_editor.gd (3): keys, paths of made-up names (as copied too), kept edits put back on a new
  one; in a game - opens, pause, a click picks a thing by its ray, its tabs, a material edit kept, a new mesh on it
  and on another of its kind, saved into a mod (edits + mesh file); a character has its clips.
  tests/test_solids_edit.gd (4): town, station, hangar, dungeon solids; the tab.

## 2026-11-24 - The mesh editor: right-click tools, gizmo, T-pose, hover wireframe, turntables, live icons

Asked (in a playtest): an extensive right-click menu of icons only with tooltips, left click for selecting, panels
resizable by dragging, a left drag in empty space turning the view, selected objects and parts outlined, the models
list as icons with previews (and the detailed list), all icons animatable (previews turning, other animations), edit
mode showing vertices and wireframe only round the hovered area, the wireframe on top of the model and always visible
in edit mode, a T-pose to make editing easier, weapons at the side and easy to hide, a move / rotate / scale gizmo.

- **The mouse**: left click selects (a part; in edit mode points / edges / faces); a left drag in empty space turns the
  view; from the model in edit mode (or Shift) it draws a selection box; right click: the menu; right drag pans.
- **The right-click menu** (menu()): icons only, each with its tooltip (name, keys, what it does), in groups for what
  can be done now - object mode: edit mode, T-pose, weapons, move / turn / scale, duplicate, rename, hide, delete; the
  six primitives; mirror X / Y / Z, apply; edit mode: vertex / edge / face, select all / none / invert, move, turn,
  scale, extrude, subdivide, merge, delete, flip, recalc normals; proportional editing, falloff, connected, symmetry
  X / Y / Z, symmetrize both ways; and always: frame, views, ortho, undo, redo, save. 42 new vector icons (m_*).
- **Resizable panels**: models / parts / view / the part's panel in split containers - each divider dragged; sizes
  kept (user://editor_layout.cfg).
- **Outlines** (SelectOutline, shaders/outline.gdshader - back faces pushed out a few pixels in screen space, any
  distance, skinned too): the mesh editor's selected part (fainter in edit mode) and the Live Editor's pick; never
  saved into a file.
- **The models list**: Icons (a picture of each, its name under it) or Details (paths, a small picture); the pictures
  are turntables - 24 frames round the model, drawn once in the background one frame a tick (mesh_thumbs.gd), kept on
  disk; the hovered one turns (TurntableHover).
- **Live icons** (IconAnim, every icon button - EditorIcons.dress, the Talos rail, the menus): hovered, the icon moves -
  spin (turn, reload), turntable (cubes, primitives, mirror), push (move, scale, frame), bob (extrude, flip, save),
  breathe (proportional, merge, effects), swing (undo, back, help), pulse with a glint (the rest); eased back on
  leaving; drawn as a transform of the same picture - nothing repainted, nothing while not hovered.
- **Edit mode's overlays**: the whole wireframe always, faint (every selection mode); the area round the mouse (a 110 px
  circle at the model, reached along the edges) bright - its edges and points fading to its rim - lifted over the
  surface and faintly through it; the selection whole. Hover tracked at most 60 times a second.
- **T-pose** (Ctrl+T): a character laid out for editing - arm bones turned straight out to their sides, its weapon's
  bone stood upright beside it - the skinned mesh baked into that pose (each vertex by its bones' blend), edited as
  plain geometry, turned back exactly (each vertex by its blend's inverse: < 0.5 mm) when saved or turned off;
  weights kept, animations as before. On a worker; undoable.
- **Weapons** (Ctrl+W): hidden, a part's weapon surfaces (by material: gun / rifle / bow / quiver / axe / sword...;
  not a gunmetal visor) are taken out into a hidden part of their own - not drawn, edited or picked; put back when
  shown and while saving (the file keeps them).
- **The gizmo** on the selection (the part; in edit mode the selected points' middle): X / Y / Z arrows move along an
  axis, rings turn about one, boxes scale along one, the centre moves freely, the outer ring scales evenly - dragged:
  the same move / turn / scale as G / R / S (proportional editing, symmetry, undo).
- Tests: tests/test_mesh_editor.gd 11 (menu icons-only with tooltips, mouse, splits, outline, list views, hover area
  and the whole faint wireframe, T-pose exact round trip, weapons hidden and saved, the gizmo moving along X only).

  quads, a cylinder quads with fan caps, a sphere quads with triangle poles; faces kept per mesh between edit

  middle within 14 px; Ctrl - no snap), a dashed preview to the mouse; Enter / Space cuts, Backspace takes the last
  point back, Esc / right-click cancels. The cut follows the surface face to face (the plane through the two points
  and the view), a point where it crosses each edge; each face is split along it into two (re-triangulated by its
  outline - no stray diagonals), its neighbours gaining the corner; new vertices mix their edge's two (position,
  normal, colour, UVs, bone weights), hard edges and seams kept. Shift+K slices right through the part (closed

  one used by the game; buttons to add, duplicate and erase variants"): an override is now a set of numbered variants,
  each a folder of its own files (art/overrides/<model path>.variants/<n>/: the glb, and a character's model.json -
  a file a variant lacks is read from the original); the latest is active (Stage3D/CosmosModels read it). The mesh
  editor's header: a variants list (Original, Variant 1, 2... - the active one marked, saved times in tooltips; pick
  to open), **Add variant** (from the original), **Duplicate variant** (the open one with unsaved edits, as the new
  latest - reactivates an older one), **Erase variant** (asks; the previous one becomes active). Saving writes the
  open variant (saving the original makes a new one); Revert deletes all variants; a model new to the game is saved
  where it's saved (nothing to override). Variants are game-side (in a mod, the mod's copy stays the override).
  ModelOverride rewritten (variants/active/add/erase/file_of/read); docs mesh-save. Test:
  test_save_is_an_override_with_variants (save, duplicate, add, erase, older variant, revert; the game's mesh at each step).

## 2026-11-24 - The mesh editor: curve deform, flatten, reference images

Asked: move many points with a curve and its handles; flatten points onto a plane; reference images behind or over
the model.

- **Curve deform** (asked; V, the EDIT MESH row, the right-click menu): a cubic curve laid straight along the
  selection, from one end of its longest extent to the other (the farthest point from the middle, the farthest
  from it; every point projected on that line), drawn over the model - two ends (squares), two handles (knobs on
  dashed lines), the hovered one lit. Drag them in the view (over the plane facing you; X / Y / Z: along an axis);
  an end takes its handle along. Each moved point keeps its offset from the straight line and is carried - and
  turned by the curve's tangent - at its place along it (0..1, clamped), so a straight row bends into the curve
  (the middle rises 3/4 of the handles' rise). A transform kind "CRV" of the editor's: proportional editing (the
  wheel: its radius), symmetry and the mirror's clipping apply, one undo step; Enter / the bar's Keep keeps,
  Esc / right-click / Cancel cancels, Straighten the curve resets it. A bar at the top of the view while it runs.
- **Flatten** (asked; Shift+Alt+F, the EDIT MESH row, the right-click menu): the selected points pressed onto a
  plane through their middle - the least-squares best fit (the covariance's smallest axis: its two largest by power
  iteration, the normal across them) or, faces selected, their area-weighted average normal; X / Y / Z (or the
  bar's buttons) the part's own axis plane. Strength 0-1 by the mouse (twice as far: all the way) or digits (1-9:
  10-90%, 0: 100%); click keeps, right-click / Esc cancels; kind "FLT", proportional editing and symmetry apply, one
  undo step. The plane's normal drawn through the middle.
- **Reference images** (asked; the REFERENCE IMAGES panel): pictures from anywhere on disk (png / jpg / webp, a
  file dialog as Import from disk's), each lined up with the front / side / top view (upright in it, centred on the
  origin, fading out as the camera turns away from it) or on a free plane (offset X/Y/Z, turn, tilt); behind the
  model (pushed to the far plane in the vertex shader: the model, grid and overlays draw over it) or over it (no
  depth test, see-through, drawn before the edit overlays); opacity, size (height in m), offset, show / hide,
  remove. Kept per model path in user://mesh_ref_images.json (saved 0.4 s after a change), back when it's opened.
  Cheap: one shared 1 x 1 quad scaled per image, one unshaded material each; pictures read (and mipmapped) on a
  worker, the tasks waited for on exit.
- Icons m_curve, m_flatten, m_ref_image; docs mesh-curve, mesh-flatten, mesh-refs; tests/test_mesh_curve.gd (5:
  the maths, curve deform with undo / cancel / proportional, a handle dragged with the mouse, flatten fit / axis
  plane / undo / cancel, reference images layers / views / saved per model).

Files: scripts/editor/mesh/deform_tools.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh/ref_images.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd,
scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_view.gd (the curve overlay), scripts/editor/editor_icons.gd, data/docs/editor.md,
tests/test_mesh_curve.gd (new).

## 2026-11-24 - The mesh editor: parts from bones

Asked: generate parts based on the bones they are associated with.

- **Parts from bones** (the PART panel's binding row - a list beside it: This bone / Bone and children / All bones -
  and three right-click menu entries): a body part for each chosen bone of a character's skeleton - the bone picked in
  Bone to bind to (Nearest: the one nearest the selected part), it and every bone below it, or every bone but the
  weapon's. Each is a closed loft (12 sides, 6 fitted rings, 3 rings rounding each end to a point) from the bone's head
  to the head of the child it points at (the child most along the bone's own axis; heads on top of it don't count),
  or for an end bone (head, fingers, foot, coat tails) as far as its vertices go along it, else a short cap. Its
  cross-sections are ellipses fitted ring by ring to the Body's vertices weighted most to that bone (at least 35%):
  centred on them, radii their 85th percentile spread along the bone's two cross axes - smoothed, kept at most 3:1,
  at least 4% of the length; with none weighted to it, 16% of its length. ~170 vertices a part.
- Each part named after its bone + "_part" (fore_L_part - a saved model's nodes share names with its bones: "fore_L"
  came back "fore_L2"), skinned 100% to its bone (it shares the Body's skin and skeleton: the game merges it into the
  Body - CosmosModels), one shared new material "Bone parts"; made where the bones are drawn now: out of the T-pose
  each vertex by the inverse of its bone's bind matrix, in the T-pose as drawn with the Body's T-pose metas (turned
  back with it on save). All the parts of one go are one undo step.
- Numbers: the pirate's 33 bones (all but the gun: 32 parts) in ~190 ms, the automaton's in ~70 ms (the Body's
  vertices gathered once, ~40k).
- Icon m_bone_parts (a bone and the rounded part grown along it); docs mesh-bone-parts; tests/test_mesh_bone_parts.gd
  (4: a bone and its children - named, all on their bone, along it, as thick as the arm, one undo step; one bone /
  all bones; in the T-pose, saved back in the own pose where the same part made out of it is; saved into a mod, read
  back with their names, merged into the Body by CosmosModels, moving with a played walk clip).

Files: scripts/editor/mesh/bone_parts.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd, scripts/editor/editor_icons.gd,
data/docs/editor.md, tests/test_mesh_bone_parts.gd (new).

## 2026-11-24 - The mesh editor: duplicate, merge by distance, inset, loop cut, select loop / ring

Asked: in edit mode, duplicate the selection (Shift+D, then move it); merge points by distance with an adjustable
threshold, and an auto merge that welds points a move puts onto others; inset faces with the mouse; then creating
edge loops (a loop cut that previews the ring of quads, cuts, then slides) and selecting edge loops (Alt+click) and
rings.

- **Duplicate** (Shift+D in edit mode - object mode keeps Shift+D for the part; the EDIT MESH row, the right-click
  menu): the whole faces the selection makes up copied - their vertices with every attribute onto new points, the
  copies' faces new ids, not joined to the old ones - selected, then a G move begins (axis locks, proportional,
  symmetry). The copy and the move are an undo step each (as Extrude): a cancelled move leaves the copy in place.
  Points / edges with no whole face copy nothing (the mesh is faces: no loose points or edges) - it says so.
- **Merge by distance** (Alt+M; the row, the menu): the selected points (all, if none) within the distance of each
  other joined (a spatial hash of cells the threshold's size, the 27 around each point, union-find), each group made
  its lowest point at the group's middle; triangles left with two corners on one point dropped, the points nothing
  uses dropped; the selection kept (renumbered). Says how many went; one undo step. Threshold: a spin box in the
  EDIT MESH panel, 0.0001 m to start (part space).
- **Auto merge** (a toggle beside it; the menu): when a move / turn / scale / spherize / inset / loop slide ends
  (confirm_transform), the points it moved within the distance of another point are welded to it - the point that
  didn't move keeps its place (moved onto moved: their middle). Part of the move's undo step.
- **Inset** (I - it was free; the row, the menu): the selected faces inset as one region - their triangles moved onto
  copies of their points and a ring of quads along the region's border (the extrude's walls, the top not lifted),
  the region's inner points renumbered away. Each border point goes in along the faces: its sides' inward
  directions met and divided by the cosine between them, so every side's ring is as wide. Width: the mouse towards
  the selection's middle (started near the middle: as far as it moves) or typed (digits, a point, Backspace); click /
  Enter keeps (one step with the new faces), right-click / Esc cancels to the mesh and selection as before. The inner
  faces selected after. A closed region (no border) says so.
- **Loop cut** (Ctrl+R - free: Ctrl+R wasn't bound; the row, the menu): pointing at an edge shows the new loop (the
  knife's line and diamonds) round the ring across it - quad to quad through the opposite sides, either way, until a
  triangle / n-gon, an open edge or round to the start. A click cuts it as one knife chain of edge nodes
  (EditMesh.knife_apply: each quad split in two, the faces where it stops get the new point as a corner, UVs /
  normals / bone weights from the edges); then the mouse along the first edge slides the loop (0-100%, each new point
  along its own side) and a click keeps it; right-click / Esc keeps it in the middle. Symmetry on: the mirror ring
  is cut too (unless it's the same ring). The new edges selected; cut + slide one undo step.
- **Select loop / ring**: Alt+click an edge (Alt+drag still orbits: a press and release within 5 px is a click;
  Shift+Alt+click adds) - its loop from both ends straight through each four-edge point (the one edge sharing no
  face with the way in), stopping at poles and open ends (an open edge's loop runs along the border), or round;
  vertex mode its points, face mode the ring of quads across the nearest edge. Select loop / Select ring (the row,
  the menu) from the selected edges; ring = the edges a loop cut would cross. Symmetry twins too.
- The editor hooks are small: a tool's transform carries "step" / "on_cancel" / "name" (_xf_update, _cancel_xf,
  confirm_transform call them), mesh_ops.after_transform before the undo step, mesh_ops.key / view_input asked
  first by the key and view handlers, one menu group, one panel row.
- Icons m_duplicate_mesh, m_merge_dist, m_auto_merge, m_inset, m_loop_cut, m_sel_loop, m_sel_ring; docs
  mesh-duplicate, mesh-merge-distance, mesh-inset, mesh-loop-cut, mesh-select-loop.
- Tests: tests/test_mesh_ops.gd (8): duplicate (none from one point, a face copied + moved, two undos), merge by
  distance (a doubled box back to 8 points, selected only, zero distance, undo), auto merge (a corner moved onto
  another welded, one undo, off), inset (typed 0.1: 4 points, 10 faces, quads, inner face selected, undo, cancel, a
  closed box refused), loop cut on a box (closed ring of 4, slid to 25%, undo, cancelled slide kept in the middle),
  on a 10 x 10 grid (open ring of 10, 11 points; with the mouse: preview of 11, click, slide, click), select loop /
  ring (10 edges / 11, the buttons, Alt+click through the view input, face mode's ring of 10 quads), the row, icons
  and menu entries.

Files: scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_ops.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd (hooks: preload + node, panel row, menu
group, keys Shift+D / I / Ctrl+R / Alt+M, the transform's step / cancel / name, auto merge on confirm, the view input),
scripts/editor/editor_icons.gd, data/docs/editor.md, tests/test_mesh_ops.gd (new).
- **Checked in a real window** (asked: "test their functionality thoroughly"), and fixed what that turned up:
  - **Merge by distance left doubled faces**: welding a copy back onto the faces it came from kept both sets (the
    points merged, the faces overlapping - 110 faces became 119). Welding now keeps one of each set of faces that end up
    on the same points (only among the faces touching merged points). test_merge_by_distance checks the box ends with
    6 faces / 12 triangles.
  - **Reference images over the model (and free planes) never showed**: their shader set the vertex position only for
    the behind-the-model case, and Godot leaves the position wholly to a shader that writes it anywhere - so the others
    were never placed. Now always set (the far-plane push on top for "behind").
  - Curve deform's and flatten's hints shortened (they ran off the view's edge).
  - Tests no longer race on the pirate's override: the variants test saves into a folder of its own
    (ModelOverride.dir, user://test_overrides/), so a test reading the pirate meanwhile sees the original.
  - Frame rate: the mesh editor holds ~725 FPS with every panel open (the right panel now ~970 of its ~1,900 draw
    calls - the new tool rows); the tour measures ~450 because it builds the 12 model previews from nothing (a fresh
    install's one-off, ~530 FPS while they're made, one 31 ms frame per character as it's first drawn).
- **Curve deform: the points snap exactly onto the curve** (asked: "in curve deform the vertices should snap exactly on
  top of the curve"): the selected points now sit on the curve itself, spaced along it by length as they were along the
  straight line (an arc-length table, 64 samples; DeformTools.curve_snap / arc_table / arc_t) - before, each kept its
  offset from the line. A **Snap onto the curve** toggle on the curve's bar (on by default) turns it off for bending an
  area with offsets kept; points pulled by proportional editing always keep theirs. Docs mesh-curve. Test:
  test_curve_snaps_points_onto_it (every point within 1 cm of the curve, the ends on its ends; off: offsets back).
- **Curve deform: the curve starts through the points** (asked: "the curve should start as a shape that passes through
  the vertices - set up its handles appropriately - so the vertices don't move unless the curve is modified"): the curve
  is fitted to the selection - its ends on the two end points (along the selection's longest extent), its handles
  solved by least squares (chord-length spacing refined by Newton steps; lightly held towards the thirds so 2-3 points
  still give a sound curve). Every affected point is bound to it: its place along it (fraction of length), its offset
  and the curve's direction there; untouched curve - no point moves; changed - the selected snap onto it (or keep their
  turned offsets with snapping off), proportional ones keep theirs. "Straighten the curve" became **Reset the curve**
  (back to the fitted start). DeformTools.fit_curve / bind_points / nearest_t / arc_f. Test:
  test_curve_starts_through_the_points (an arc: nothing moves, the curve within 5 mm of every point, a tiny nudge moves
  them under 1 cm, Reset puts them back).
- **Curve deform with faces selected carries the faces** (asked: "if faces are selected then the curve affects the
  faces"): in face mode (or Auto with whole faces picked) the curve is fitted through the selected faces' middles and
  every point of them keeps its offset, turned with the curve - the faces bend along it whole instead of their corners
  collapsing onto it (no snapping there); the hint says "Curve deform: the faces". DeformTools.face_centres. Test:
